title: distribution-channel conformance case
description: One call into the distribution-channel battery. `kind` selects the function; the inputs and the shape of `expect` follow from it. Each branch requires its own inputs AND forbids the other kind's, so a case carrying a member that belongs to the other function fails validation rather than running against an absent argument.

channel.description: §1's closed set. A binding must not accept, resolve to, or emit a hint for any other value.

asciiPath.description: Printable ASCII only. §3 lowercases the whole path, and Go's simple case mapping disagrees with Python's and JavaScript's full one on U+0130 — so a non-ASCII path would pin a value the three bindings do not share.

env.description: resolve: the injected environment map. Always present — never omitted — because an absent option makes the reference implementation read process.env and test the runner's own machine.

realpath.description: resolve: the injected symlink resolver, as data. A key maps to its resolved path; a key mapping to NULL means the resolver THROWS for that path, which is the only way §3.1 is pinnable — a map alone can express only a resolver that succeeds. A path absent from the map resolves to itself.

channel.description: null is a normal, expected result (§R6): the plain direct-download install, where the self-updater stays enabled.

text.description: §4: contract text, byte for byte. A binding returning the right meaning in different words does not conform.
